answer: One identity, one past — that is the whole test. Land registry deed with title office attestation is the past in question: a deed recorded decades ago in the national land registry. The opal here is the registry itself, a book the applicant never held and cannot rewrite. A farm wanting a hundred accounts must forge a hundred such books, and the sonnet of each forgery is the years it pretends to contain. The island that ends the check is a single phone call to the keeper of the record.
